risk: A stolen Ezra key = full control of the account
remediation: Daily admin through an MFA-protected admin role (assume-role); remove direct AdministratorAccess and the redundant SecurityAudit/inline policies (I-1)

risk: Same root cause as F-01: a '*:*' policy is in use
remediation: Closed together with F-01 (admin role instead of user attachment)

risk: Root protected by a phone (virtual) MFA, not a hardware key
remediation: Exception EXC-L03: virtual MFA, no root access keys, root not used; buy a FIDO2 key for production

risk: Long-lived access keys work until revoked (2 already leaked during setup, incident I-3)
remediation: Auditor: switch to role conote-security-audit (already deployed); 90-day key rotation meanwhile

risk: Nothing stops a bucket from being made public account-wide
remediation: Exception EXC-L01 until the final challenge is done, then enable: aws s3control put-public-access-block (all 4 true)

risk: Root used on 2026-11-18 for account set-up
remediation: Expected during set-up; no further root use. Check clears automatically; verify in next scan

risk: New instances could start with IMDSv1 (credential theft via SSRF); current instance already requires IMDSv2
remediation: aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-defaults --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 1

risk: Only one network layer (security groups) protects the hosts
remediation: Custom NACL on the conote subnet: allow 80/443 + ephemeral ports, deny the rest

risk: Web ports open to the internet
remediation: Intended public web service (tag Exposure=public-intended). Exception EXC-L04; production = ALB + WAF

risk: If the public server is compromised, its role credentials can be used
remediation: Role limited to AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore; production = private subnet behind ALB (EXC-L05, cost)

risk: Trust policy has no aws:SourceAccount/SourceArn condition
remediation: Add Condition StringEquals aws:SourceAccount=093397426920 to the trust policy (Terraform)

risk: Alert messages stored unencrypted at rest
remediation: EXC-L02. Possible fix: customer-managed KMS key whose policy allows events & cloudwatch

risk: No backup of the server disk
remediation: AWS Backup plan, daily snapshot, 7-day retention

risk: Virtual MFA only; auditor has no console so MFA does not apply
remediation: Covered by EXC-L03 (virtual MFA); auditor has no password

risk: Org-level guardrails (SCP region deny, tag policies) unavailable
remediation: Not applicable: single Free-plan account (joining an Organization upgrades to Paid). Mute in Prowler mutelist

risk: Weak console passwords allowed
remediation: aws iam update-account-password-policy --minimum-password-length 14 --require-symbols --require-numbers --require-uppercase-characters --require-lowercase-characters --password-reuse-prevention 24 --max-password-age 90

risk: Root use, failed logins, IAM/CloudTrail/KMS changes raise no alert
remediation: Send CloudTrail to CloudWatch Logs + metric filters & alarms (start with root usage, unauthorized calls, console without MFA, IAM policy changes). SG/S3 changes already covered by the EventBridge rule

risk: No configuration history (who changed what, before/after)
remediation: Enable AWS Config recorder in eu-west-1 (small cost) or keep CloudTrail+CSPM as compensating control

risk: No automatic detection of resources shared outside the account
remediation: aws accessanalyzer create-analyzer --analyzer-name conote-analyzer --type ACCOUNT (free)

risk: Permissions managed per user, hard to review
remediation: Group cspm-auditors holding the audit policies; admin through role (F-01)

risk: AWS cannot reach a security contact during an incident
remediation: Account > Alternate contacts > Security: set name, email, phone

risk: SSE-S3 instead of KMS keys; deletion not protected by MFA/object lock
remediation: Exception EXC-L06: AES-256 + versioning + private + TLS-only; MFA delete needs root, object lock only at bucket creation

risk: Flow logs encrypted with AWS-owned key; 30-day retention below the checked minimum
remediation: KMS key on the log group; retention 365 days

risk: Single AZ, no private tier, no VPC endpoints
remediation: Lab design decision D2 (cost); production = 2 AZs, private app subnet, endpoints

risk: Not applicable: no AI services deployed (noise)
remediation: Mute in Prowler mutelist with justification

risk: SSH reachable from the whole internet (brute force, exploitation)
remediation: Custodian remediate-public-ssh-access (remove-permissions: matched) with MFA role, change CHG-001

risk: No record of who read or wrote which object (data exfiltration invisible)
remediation: CloudTrail data events for S3 (at least uploads + backups, write events first: low volume)

risk: No data classification and no central findings hub
remediation: Cost decision for the lab (Security Hub/Macie are paid after trial); Prowler + Powerpipe + register act as the findings hub. Reconsider in production

risk: Traffic in the unused default VPC is not logged
remediation: Delete the default VPC (preferred, also closes R3 and 5.5) or enable flow logs

risk: No dedicated role to manage AWS Support cases during an incident
remediation: Role with AWSSupportAccess, assumable by the admin

risk: SSH reachable from the internet (M6 controlled alert test)
remediation: Custodian remediate-public-ssh-access with MFA role, change CHG-002
